title: Extend compact smooth LSI to the noncompact smooth analytic domain
source_anchor: Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling, Section 2.1.1, printed pp. 48–49 / PDF pp. 60–61; compact-test LSI and density extension; consumer Exercise 1.7, printed p. 43 / PDF p. 55
target_statement: In finite dimension a function-form LSI for all compact C∞ tests extends with the same coefficient 2C to globally smooth tests in the explicit mass, genuine gradient energy and entropy-integrable domain. No sign of C, normalized mass or finite measure is imposed.
consumers: AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.CompactLogSobolevPoincare.variance_le_of_compact_logSobolev applies it to the actual smooth square-root perturbation
Chewi §2.1.1 density passage on the stated sufficient analytic domain

statement_seal.definition_kind: Literal function-form real Bochner integrals; genuine Hilbert gradient on smooth tests.
statement_seal.binder_audit: Finite dimension supplies compactness of cutoff support. The three target integrability premises are sufficient domain predicates and are proved inside the Exercise 1.7 consumer.

source_gaps: Compact smooth tests are not automatically integrable for arbitrary measures. The compact premise is totalized; actual cutoff products are integrable from the explicit analytic hypotheses.
excluded_with_reason: A sufficient smooth-domain extension. For arbitrary Borel measures the compact premise is a statement using Mathlib's totalized Bochner integrals; it is not a claim that classical entropy is defined on every compact smooth test. The actual cutoff tests used in the proof have genuine integrable terms. This is not the full closed Dirichlet-form domain, the Poincare conclusion, or a new assumption on the final compact PI theorem.
